But how far this is! Perhaps what led its proponent to it is His words: ﴿and We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾, since the pronoun refers to the Book.

It has also been said: The pronoun in "his meeting" refers to the return (al-rujू') understood from His words: ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned﴾ [al-Sajdah: 11]. That is, do not be in doubt about meeting the return. This too is far-fetched.

There is a difference of opinion regarding the pronoun in His words ﴿and We made it﴾. It has been said that it refers to the Book, meaning: We made the Torah a guidance for the Children of Israel. This was said by al-Hasan and others.

Qatadah said: It refers to Moses, meaning: We made Moses a guidance for the Children of Israel.

﴿And We made from among them imams﴾, meaning leaders whom they follow in their religion. The Kufans read "a'immatan" (with two hamzahs). Al-Nahhas said: This is a solecism (lahn) according to all the grammarians, because it combines two hamzahs in one word. The meaning of ﴿who guided by Our command﴾ is: they call them to guidance by what they convey to them of the rulings and admonitions of the Torah, by Our command, meaning by Our command to them to do so, or for the sake of Our command.

Qatadah said: By the imams is meant the prophets among them.

It has also been said: They are scholars.

﴿When they were patient﴾. The majority read "lamma" with a fatha on the lam and a shaddah on the mim, meaning "when they were patient." The pronoun refers to the imams, and "lamma" carries the sense of a condition, with the implied meaning: when they were patient, We made them imams. This patience is their patience under the hardships of obligation and of guiding people. It has also been said: They were patient regarding the world, and they were certain of Our revelatory signs (ayat al-tanzil), meaning they affirmed them and knew that they are truth and from Allah, because of their intense reflection and abundant contemplation.

﴿Indeed your Lord, He will judge between them﴾, meaning He will decide between them and judge between the believers and the disbelievers ﴿on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾. It has also been said: He will decide between the prophets and their nations. This was related by al-Naqqash.

﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾, meaning has it not been made clear to them? The hamzah is for denial (inkar), and the subject (fa'il) is what is indicated by ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them﴾, meaning: Has it not been made clear to them the great number of those We destroyed before them?

Al-Farra' said: "kam" is in the nominative position with "yahdi".

Al-Mubarrad said: The subject is the guidance indicated by "yahdi", meaning: Has guidance not been made clear to them?

Al-Zajjaj said: "kam" is in the accusative position governed by "ahlakna" (We destroyed).

By "the generations" is meant ʿAd, Thamud and the like. The clause ﴿they walk in their dwellings﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in "lahum", meaning: while they walk in the dwellings of those who were destroyed, and see them, and observe the lessons and traces of punishment in them, yet they take no heed. It has also been said that it refers to the destroyed, and the meaning is: We destroyed them while they were walking in their dwellings. The first is preferable.

﴿Indeed in that are signs, great ones. Will they not then hear?﴾, meaning will they not hear them and be admonished by them?

﴿Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land﴾, meaning have they not known by Our driving the water to the land that does not grow anything except by driving water to it? It has also been said: It is the dry land. Its origin is from jarz, which means cutting, i.e., land whose growth has been cut off due to lack of water. "Juruz" is not said of land that produces nothing at all, such as salt flats, because of His words: ﴿so We bring forth thereby crops﴾. It has been said: It is the land of Yemen. It has been said: It is the land of Aden.

al-Dahhak said: It is the thirsty land.

al-Farra' said: It is the land in which there is no vegetation.

al-Asma'i said: It is the land that grows nothing.

al-Mubarrad said: It is unlikely that the land itself is meant, because of the presence of the definite article (al-). It has been said that it is derived from the saying of the Arabs, "rajul jaruz", when a man leaves nothing without eating it. From this is the verse of the rajaz poet:

A glutton (khibb) who is greedy (jaruz), and when hungry he weeps,
and eats dates and does not leave the pits.

Likewise a she-camel is called jaruz when she eats everything she finds.

Mujahid said: It is the land of the Nile, because the water comes to it every year. ﴿So We bring forth thereby﴾, meaning by the water, ﴿crops from which eat their livestock﴾, meaning from the crops such as straw, leaves and the like, which people do not eat, ﴿and themselves﴾, meaning they eat the grains that emerge from the crops, of what they subsist on. The clause ﴿from which eat their livestock﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause. ﴿Will they not then see?﴾ These blessings, and thank the Bestower and affirm His oneness, because He alone is the one who brings all this into existence.

﴿And they say, "When is this victory, if you are truthful?"﴾ The ones who say this are the disbelievers in general, or specifically the disbelievers of Makkah. The meaning is: When is the victory that you promise us? By "victory" they mean the judgment and the decision between the servants, which is the Day of Resurrection on which Allah judges between His servants. This was said by Mujahid and others.

al-Farra' and al-Qutaybi said: It is the conquest of Makkah.

Qatadah said: The Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the disbelievers: For us there is a day in which we will be blessed and rest, and Allah will judge between us and you, meaning the Day of Resurrection. The disbelievers then said, "When is this victory?"

The meaning of ﴿nor will they be reprieved﴾ is: they will not be given respite nor delayed. "Yawma" in "yawm al-fath" is in the accusative as an adverb of time, and al-Farra' permitted the nominative.

﴿So turn away from them﴾, meaning from their foolishness and denial, and do not answer them except with what you have been commanded, ﴿and wait, indeed they are waiting﴾, meaning wait for the day of victory, which is the Day of Resurrection, or the day of their destruction by killing; indeed they are waiting for you to face the events of time, such as death, killing or defeat. It has also been said that it is not abrogated, since turning away may occur together with the command to fight.

Abu Hatim said: The correct reading is with a kasrah, meaning: wait for their punishment; indeed they are waiting for your destruction.

I saw 'Isa ibn Maryam, of medium build, inclining to redness and whiteness, with straight hair. And I saw Malik, the keeper of Hell, and al-Dajjal, among the signs which Allah showed me." He said: [He recited] ﴿So do not be in doubt about meeting him﴾. Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah related with a chain which al-Suyuti described as sahih, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿So do not be in doubt about meeting him﴾, that he said: "It is the meeting with Musa." al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir: The chain from Ibn Abbas is sahih, with no flaw in it.

al-Hakim related and declared it sahih, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il (Dala'il al-Nubuwwah) related from Ibn Abbas concerning His words ﴿And they say, "When is this victory, if you are truthful?"﴾ that he said: "It is the day of Badr. It has been said: It is the land of Aden.

al-Dahhak said: It is the thirsty land.

al-Farra' said: It is the land in which there is no vegetation.

al-Asma'i said: It is the land that grows nothing.

al-Mubarrad said: It is unlikely that the land itself is meant, because of the presence of the definite article (al-). It has been said that it is derived from the saying of the Arabs, "rajul jaruz", when a man leaves nothing without eating it. From this is the verse of the rajaz poet:

A glutton (khibb) who is greedy (jaruz), and when hungry he weeps,
and eats dates and does not leave the pits.

Likewise a she-camel is called jaruz when she eats everything she finds.

The clause ﴿from which eat their livestock﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause. ﴿Will they not then see?﴾ These blessings, and thank the Bestower and affirm His oneness, because He alone is the one who brings all this into existence.

The meaning is: When is the victory that you promise us? al-Farra' and al-Qutaybi said: It is the conquest of Makkah.

﴿So turn away from them﴾, meaning from their foolishness and denial, and do not answer them except with what you have been commanded, ﴿and wait, indeed they are waiting﴾, meaning wait for the day of victory, which is the Day of Resurrection, or the day of their destruction by killing; indeed they are waiting for you to face the events of time, such as death, killing or defeat. It has also been said that it is not abrogated, since turning away may occur together with the command to fight.

al-Farra' said: This is not valid except with an implied element, meaning: they are awaited.

Abu Hatim said: The correct reading is with a kasrah, meaning: wait for their punishment; indeed they are waiting for your destruction.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others related from the hadith of Ibn Abbas who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I saw Musa ibn 'Imran, a tall man with curly hair, as if he were one of the men of Shanu'ah. al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir: The chain from Ibn Abbas is sahih, with no flaw in it.

The meaning of ﴿nor will they be reprieved﴾ is: they will not be given respite nor delayed. "Yawma" in "yawm al-fath" is in the accusative as an adverb of time, and al-Farra' permitted the nominative.

﴿So turn away from them﴾, meaning from their foolishness and denial, and do not answer them except with what you have been commanded, ﴿and wait, indeed they are waiting﴾, meaning wait for the day of victory, which is the Day of Resurrection, or the day of their destruction by killing; indeed they are waiting for you to face the events of time, such as death, killing or defeat. This is like His words: ﴿So wait, indeed We are with you among those who wait﴾ [al-Tawbah: 52]. It is also possible that it means they are waiting for their own destruction. The verse is abrogated (mansukhah, i.e., by naskh) by the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf). It has also been said that it is not abrogated, since turning away may occur together with the command to fight.

al-Farra' said: This is not valid except with an implied element, meaning: they are awaited.

Abu Hatim said: The correct reading is with a kasrah, meaning: wait for their punishment; indeed they are waiting for your destruction.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others related from the hadith of Ibn Abbas who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I saw Musa ibn 'Imran, a tall man with curly hair, as if he were one of the men of Shanu'ah. I saw 'Isa ibn Maryam, of medium build, inclining to redness and whiteness, with straight hair. And I saw Malik, the keeper of Hell, and al-Dajjal, among the signs which Allah showed me." He said: [He recited] ﴿So do not be in doubt about meeting him﴾. Qatadah used to explain it as meaning that the Prophet (ﷺ) had met Moses, and [about] ﴿and We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾, he said: Allah made Moses a guidance for the Children of Israel.

Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah related with a chain which al-Suyuti described as sahih, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿So do not be in doubt about meeting him﴾, that he said: "It is the meeting with Musa." It was said: Did he meet Musa? He said: "Yes. Do you not see His words: ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 45]?"

Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas concerning His words ﴿Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land﴾ that he said: "The juruz are those which are not rained upon except with a rain that does not benefit them, except what comes to them from torrents."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him concerning His words ﴿to the barren land﴾ that he said: "It is a land in Yemen."

al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir: The chain from Ibn Abbas is sahih, with no flaw in it.

al-Hakim related and declared it sahih, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il (Dala'il al-Nubuwwah) related from Ibn Abbas concerning His words ﴿And they say, "When is this victory, if you are truthful?"﴾ that he said: "It is the day of Badr. Victory was granted to the Prophet (ﷺ), and their faith did not benefit those who disbelieved after death."

(p. 1154) Concerning His words, ﴿And We gave Moses the Book﴾, meaning the Torah, ﴿so do not be in doubt about meeting him﴾, meaning do not be in suspicion or uncertainty about meeting him. Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes (mufassirun) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was promised that he would meet Moses before he died, and then he met him in the heavens or in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) when he was taken on the Night Journey (al-Isra').

This is the view of Mujahid, al-Kalbi and al-Suddi.

It has also been said: ﴿So do not be in doubt about meeting Moses﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, and you will meet him there.

It has also been said: ﴿So do not be in doubt about meeting Moses﴾ regarding the Book. This was said by al-Zajjaj. Al-Hasan said that its meaning is: We gave Moses the Book, and he was denied and harmed, so do not be in doubt that you will meet what Moses met of denial and harm. In this case the pronoun in "his meeting" refers to something omitted, and the meaning is: the meeting of what Moses encountered.

Al-Nahhas said: This is a strange view.

It has also been said: There is a transposition (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the speech, and the meaning is: Say, "The Angel of Death who has been assigned to you will take you," so do not be in doubt about meeting him. Thus the phrase came as an interjection between ﴿And We gave Moses the Book﴾ and ﴿and We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾.

It has also been said: The pronoun refers to the Book, which is the Criterion (al-Furqan), as in His words: ﴿And indeed you receive the Qur'an﴾ [al-Naml: 6]. The meaning is: We gave Moses the like of what We gave you of the Book, and We gave him the like of what We gave you of revelation, so do not be in doubt that you have received its like and its equivalent. It has also been said: The pronoun in "his meeting" refers to the return (al-rujू') understood from His words: ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned﴾ [al-Sajdah: 11]. That is, do not be in doubt about meeting the return. This too is far-fetched.

Qatadah said: It refers to Moses, meaning: We made Moses a guidance for the Children of Israel.

﴿And We made from among them imams﴾, meaning leaders whom they follow in their religion. The Kufans read "a'immatan" (with two hamzahs). Al-Nahhas said: This is a solecism (lahn) according to all the grammarians, because it combines two hamzahs in one word. Qatadah said: By the imams is meant the prophets among them.

It has also been said: They are scholars.

Abu 'Ubayd chose this reading, citing the reading of Ibn Mas'ud "bima sabaru" with the letter ba'.

This patience is their patience under the hardships of obligation and of guiding people. It has also been said: They were patient regarding the world, and they were certain of Our revelatory signs (ayat al-tanzil), meaning they affirmed them and knew that they are truth and from Allah, because of their intense reflection and abundant contemplation.

﴿Indeed your Lord, He will judge between them﴾, meaning He will decide between them and judge between the believers and the disbelievers ﴿on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾. It has also been said: He will decide between the prophets and their nations. This was related by al-Naqqash.

﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾, meaning has it not been made clear to them? The hamzah is for denial (inkar), and the subject (fa'il) is what is indicated by ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them﴾, meaning: Has it not been made clear to them the great number of those We destroyed before them?

Al-Farra' said: "kam" is in the nominative position with "yahdi".

Al-Mubarrad said: The subject is the guidance indicated by "yahdi", meaning: Has guidance not been made clear to them?

Al-Zajjaj said: "kam" is in the accusative position governed by "ahlakna" (We destroyed).

It has also been said that it refers to the destroyed, and the meaning is: We destroyed them while they were walking in their dwellings. The first is preferable.

﴿Indeed in that are signs, great ones. Will they not then hear?﴾, meaning will they not hear them and be admonished by them?

Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah related with a chain which al-Suyuti described as sahih, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿So do not be in doubt about meeting him﴾, that he said: "It is the meeting with Musa." It was said: Did he meet Musa? He said: "Yes. Do you not see His words: ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 45]?"

Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas concerning His words ﴿Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land﴾ that he said: "The juruz are those which are not rained upon except with a rain that does not benefit them, except what comes to them from torrents."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him concerning His words ﴿to the barren land﴾ that he said: "It is a land in Yemen."

al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir: The chain from Ibn Abbas is sahih, with no flaw in it.

al-Hakim related and declared it sahih, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il (Dala'il al-Nubuwwah) related from Ibn Abbas concerning His words ﴿And they say, "When is this victory, if you are truthful?"﴾ that he said: "It is the day of Badr. Victory was granted to the Prophet (ﷺ), and their faith did not benefit those who disbelieved after death."
